record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: How can federated learning provide strong protection against an adversarial server, including efficient verifiability through zero-knowledge proofs or trusted execution environments and practical exploit-resistant TEE platforms with trustworthy links between attested binaries and privacy properties?

evidence.quote: Strong protection against an adversarial server

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning protocol in which a central server orchestrates training over data held privately by $n$ clients. In each round $t$, every participating client $i$ holds a local dataset $D_i$ and computes an update $u_i^{(t)} = \mathcal{U}(	heta^{(t)}, D_i)$ based on the current global model $	heta^{(t)}$. The server aggregates updates via a function $A$ and broadcasts $	heta^{(t+1)} = A(\{u_i^{(t)}\}_i, 	heta^{(t)})$. Assume the server is fully adversarial: it may deviate arbitrarily from the protocol, fabricate messages, equivocate between clients, and attempt to extract information about any $D_i$ beyond what is revealed by the final model.

Design and analyze a federated learning protocol that simultaneously satisfies all of the following:

1. (Privacy) For every client $i$, the joint view of the server and any colluding set $S \subseteq [n] \setminus \{i\}$ of other clients reveals no more information about $D_i$ than that implied by an agreed differential-privacy budget $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ applied to the released global model.

2. (Efficient verifiability) Every client can verify, in time and communication that is sublinear in $n$ and polynomial in the security parameter $\lambda$, that the server honestly executed $A$ on the actual client inputs of that round. The verification mechanism must be realizable either through a succinct zero-knowledge proof system applied to $A$, or through a trusted execution environment (TEE) whose remote attestation cryptographically links the attested binary to a formally specified privacy property.

3. (Exploit resistance) The TEE-based instantiation must remain secure against the class of known side-channel and microarchitectural attacks on commodity TEE platforms, with an explicit reduction from protocol security to clearly stated hardware assumptions.

4. (Trustworthy binding) Provide a formal definition and a construction that establishes a verifiable link between the attested binary (or proof statement) running on the server and the privacy property promised to clients, such that no efficient adversary can produce an accepting transcript while violating the privacy property except with negligible probability in $\lambda$.

Either construct such a protocol with proofs of the four properties above and an asymptotic analysis of its per-round computation and communication costs, or prove an impossibility result identifying which subset of (1)–(4) cannot be simultaneously achieved under standard cryptographic and hardware assumptions.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a broad open research direction in federated learning, encompassing zero-knowledge proof aggregation and TEE-based verifiable training. Subsequent work (e.g., zkFL, RoFL, Flamingo, GuardFL, and TEE-aided FL systems) has produced partial constructions for verifiable aggregation and TEE-protected training, but no single protocol simultaneously achieves efficient verifiability, exploit-resistant TEEs, and a formally proven binding to privacy properties; numerous side-channel attacks on SGX/TDX have continued to appear. The overall problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: zkFL: Zero-Knowledge Proof-based Gradient Aggregation for Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a ZK-proof-based verifiable aggregation scheme for FL, addressing malicious server behavior but with overhead and limited DP integration.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on ZK-verifiable aggregation against malicious servers exists but does not solve the full problem.

status_evidence.title: RoFL: Robustness of Secure Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Provides cryptographically enforced norm constraints on client updates under a malicious server, but does not provide succinct verifiability of arbitrary aggregation.
status_evidence.claim: Existing protocols achieve only subsets of the desired properties.

status_evidence.title: SoK: TEEs for Confidential Computing and ML
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys numerous side-channel and microarchitectural attacks on commodity TEEs, indicating that exploit-resistant TEE platforms remain an open challenge.
status_evidence.claim: Practical exploit-resistant TEEs with formal binding to privacy properties are not yet available.
